The Committee's view of inflation worsened between 2021 and 2022. Inflation remained elevated, with total PCE inflation at 6.2% over the 12 months ending September 2022 and core PCE inflation at 5.1% during the same period [2022-11-02/staffEconomy/3]. Earlier, in July 2022, core PCE inflation was 4.6% [2022-09-21/staffEconomy/3]. By late 2022, inflation expectations had risen to 2.27%, up from 2.16% three months earlier and 2.3% a year earlier [2022-12-30]. The Committee expressed concern that elevated inflation could raise public expectations beyond the target, making future policy harder [2021-12-15/participantsViews/9].

The Committee's view of the labor market worsened between 2008 and 2009. In December 2008, it noted that payroll employment fell rapidly across many industries, including manufacturing, construction, retail, and financial services [2008-12-16/staffEconomy/2]. By June 2009, participants still viewed labor market conditions as a major concern, with substantial job losses and a rapidly rising unemployment rate [2009-06-24/participantsViews/6]. The unemployment rate rose from 6.8% in 2008 to 10% in November 2009, and jobless claims increased from 533,000 in 2008 to 468,000 in December 2009, indicating a deteriorating situation [2009-12-31/the unemployment rate][2009-12-31/weekly jobless claims].

The Committee's view of interest rate policy evolved from a low rate to a higher, stable target between 2015 and 2018. It began at 0 to 1/4 percent in 2015, with 9 increases and 23 holds, ending at 2-1/4 to 2-1/2 percent by 2018 [2018-12-19/policyAction/1]. Dissenting votes were present, with 4 for lower rates and 8 for higher rates, reflecting ongoing debate [2017-12-13/policyAction/15][2016-11-02/policyAction/17]. No cuts occurred during this period. The policy remained accommodative throughout, with consistent emphasis on moderate inflation and labor market strength.
